heading.en: A holy lake and a grim town

hook.en: Sometimes the most sacred places sit next to the dreariest ones. Near holy Lake Mansarovar, the writer reaches a town he finds deeply depressing.

objectives.en: Contrast Lake Mansarovar with the town of Hor
Describe the writer's illness and treatment at Darchen
Explain how the journey ends with the kora about to begin

narration.en: Sometimes the most sacred places sit next to the dreariest ones. Near holy Lake Mansarovar, the writer reaches a town he finds deeply depressing.

title.en: The sacred lake and the dreary town

body.en: Near Lake Mansarovar, revered by Hindus and Buddhists alike, the travellers stop at Hor, a dusty, bleak town with litter, harsh wind and no greenery. The writer is struck by the contrast between the beauty and holiness of the lake and the ugliness of the town. This contrast is a key descriptive technique of the chapter.

points.en: Lake Mansarovar: beautiful, sacred, a place of pilgrimage
Contrast heightens the effect of both

narration.en: Near Lake Mansarovar, revered by Hindus and Buddhists alike, the travellers stop at Hor, a dusty, bleak town with litter, harsh wind and no greenery. The writer is struck by the contrast between the beauty and holiness of the lake and the ugliness of the town. This contrast is a key descriptive technique of the chapter.
A two-column table helps us see how the writer sets the holy lake against the grim town.

say.en: Lake Mansarovar is sacred; the town beside it has no sense of holiness at all.
The lake is clear and beautiful; Hor is dusty and littered.
The lake lifts the writer's spirit, while Hor depresses him.
Pilgrims come for the lake; Hor is only a stop on the way.

body.en: At Darchen, the base town for the kora, the writer's cold and the effects of altitude grow worse, and he consults a doctor of Tibetan medicine who reassures him and gives him herbal medicine. Darchen feels empty because the main pilgrim season has not begun. His spirits lift when he knows Norbu will walk the kora with him.

points.en: Darchen: starting point of the kora
Treatment: a Tibetan doctor and herbal medicine
Ending: hope, companionship, the kora about to begin

problem.en: How does the writer contrast Lake Mansarovar with the town of Hor?

steps.en: Lake: sacred, beautiful, a goal for pilgrims.
Hor: dusty, littered, windswept and grim.
Effect: the contrast makes the town seem even more depressing to the writer.

answer.en: Lake Mansarovar appears sacred and beautiful, a goal of pilgrims, while nearby Hor is dusty, littered and bleak. The contrast deepens the writer's disappointment with the town and shows how the holy and the ordinary sit side by side.
